items.title: Roscoe Mitchell interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 23, 2023
items.q: I remember some things from Billy Taylor, you know, Lester Young, and on and on. Charlie Parker of course.

ctx.x: Was there moments of, “All right, Roscoe, come and listen to this.” Did he have people that he chose for you to hear back then?

Well I mean yeah, he had his list, but more on that side was my brother Norman. Norman, he had all these 78 records, and he called them “killers.” He’d say, “Come on over here bruh” and listen to this and listen to that and so on. And that kind of thing. I don’t know if you’re familiar with the saxophonist Nicky Hill? He was a prominent saxophonist in Chicago you know, and he was friends with Nicky Hill. And he was a very good scatter, you know, a very good scatter. So I would listen to him do that. But he had…

I can recall sort of a realization as I was listening to jazz back when I was about your age and starting to sort out the way the music worked, the accompanist, the soloist, maybe starting to realize about song form. Do you recall that sort of realization coming to you?
